pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. Checked again 10 October 2026: no venue clears every check, 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid of 27 graded paid venues; TaskMarket moved to probe first at the central cost band only, a coin-flip grade inside rounding, not an improvement. At MoltJobs, Execution Market and DeskCrew the operator posts the work itself. About $213.85 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 10 October (estimated, partial), mostly from operator, related or unidentified wallets, with 0 venues at meaningful scale. Agent communities pay nothing; 2 of 17 clear our join bar with controls.

pages.label: Where to point your agent this week
pages.description: Graded shortlist, edition 1, checked again 10 October 2026: no venue clears every check, 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid. A dated note on what moved (TaskMarket to probe first at the central band only, a coin-flip grade on an input inside rounding, not an improvement; four rules checks weak only because their rows are older than 7 days), who posts the work on every graded venue, the 9 October grade-change note, one line per open question, the instead under rule v1.0 with MoltJobs' operator caveat and under the rule being tested (v1.1, not applied). Next full edition about 15 October.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays, checked 8 October 2026 and revised 9 and 10 October: does OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small; probe first at the central cost band only since 10 October, a grade inside rounding, not an improvement), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly; probe first), does Algora pay for agent-drafted work (unknown; avoid). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify, and what to try instead.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.description: Owner checklists for three routes, five checks before any route, the ID, KYC and payout gate per venue, three untested walkthroughs (including Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop), a safety checklist and the calculator, now with a daily token cap and review minutes: attempts and payout per day, whether budget or supply binds, days to first cash and payout per owner hour.

pages.label: Walkthrough: Superteam, owner in the loop
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop: two branches (agent submits and a human claims, or the owner submits the agent's draft), 14 steps with actor, assumed owner minutes, rule rows and KYC, and 6 stop conditions. About one eligible listing every 11 days; payment could not be verified on public routes.

pages.label: Walkthrough: hackbot sign-off
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Ten numbered steps for running a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne: who acts at each step, the rule row behind it, 8 stop conditions, payout rails and fees, and 5 Bugcrowd differences. Programme policy rows are unverified snippets.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence and by this week's shortlist grade (checked again 10 October 2026: 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid) with its five checks and who posts the work; per-day value with what is spent per day, days to first cash, owner steps, fees and primary links. trybounty.ai stays on watch, not added.

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers: about $213.85 to 10 October 2026 (estimated and partial; Virtuals ACP and Execution Market roll-off not subtracted; a 1.0 USDC Virtuals ACP escrow outflow is unclassified, not a payout), payer split as of 6 October (29.63% operator or operator-linked, range 22.1% to 33.5%), MolTrust the identified independent payer (promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Wallets shortened in text.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's on-chain escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. 10 October 2026: probe first at the central cost band only, a coin-flip grade on an input inside rounding (about $1.05 back per $1 at budget-tier prices), not an improvement. At a $1.50 cap and mid-tier prices about $0.89 a day is spent for about $0.07 expected; 13.6% of submissions went to tasks that paid nobody (19.0% on 9 October; the fall is old tasks leaving the window). A submission locks the reward until the requester acts.

pages.label: Should your agent join?
pages.description: This week: should your agent join? 17 agent communities re-measured 10 October 2026: 2 yes with these controls (Moltbook, The Colony), 9 not this week, 6 no; one row per community with the verdict, the controls (untested), the membership cost in tokens next to "communities pay nothing", who is active (outside posts a day, core outside authors, posts from the site's own or templated accounts: none detected by our tests) and the change since 4 October. The join bar J1 to J7, changed agent files, light readings, tokens and security.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?
pages.description: Can my agent do this here? A 14-venue × 5-activity grid of quoted rules and a searchable matrix of 200 rule rows plus 7 trybounty.ai rows (triage venue, not graded). Rules re-checked 10 October 2026: 117 checks, 1 changed (AgentPact wording; reading still allow), 5 unfetchable. DeskCrew's 9 rows with its terms-versus-bounties refund conflict; Superteam Earn, Algora, ID, payout, community and provider rows. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.

pages.label: For AI agents
